# 釋氏通鑑

**Original Category:** 史傳部／編年通史
**Byline:** 宋 本覺編集
**Dynasty:** 宋
**Date:** 960–1279
**Juans:** 12
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/X1516

## Contributors
- 本覺 (A000260)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A late-Sòng Buddhist universal history in twelve juan, compiled by the monk [本覺](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%AC%E8%A6%BA) (Běnjué) and dated by his preface to 1270 (Sòng *Xiánchún* 咸淳 6) — within a year of [志磐](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BF%97%E7%A3%90)'s presentation of [KR6r0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0012). The title *Shìshì tōngjiàn* deliberately evokes the great Confucian universal history *Zīzhì tōngjiàn* 資治通鑑 of [司馬光](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8F%B8%E9%A6%AC%E5%85%89) (Sīmǎ Guāng), making this the first explicit Buddhist historiographical analogue to that monumental work. Preserved in the *Manji Xuzangjing* (X76 no. 1516).

**Abstract**

[本覺](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%AC%E8%A6%BA)'s preface lays out the work's plan: to compile a year-by-year annalistic chronicle of Buddhist history from the Hàn through the Southern Sòng, modelled on the *Zīzhì tōngjiàn* of [司馬光](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8F%B8%E9%A6%AC%E5%85%89) but with the Buddhist *sānbǎo* 三寶 ("Three Jewels") as its subject. Each year-entry follows the *Tōngjiàn* convention: imperial reign-year heading, brief secular annal, then Buddhist events for that year. Sources include earlier Buddhist universal histories ([KR6r0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0011), [KR6q0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0003) and other Chán lamp records, biographical compendia, and standard Buddhist sūtra catalogs), supplemented by the standard Confucian dynastic histories.

[本覺](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%AC%E8%A6%BA) himself is otherwise obscure; the autobiographical preface gives little beyond the dated colophon. The dating of 1270 is secure from this preface. The work was preserved primarily in the Jiāxīng 嘉興 reprint of the late Míng (the *Jiāxīng zàng*) and from there entered the Manji Xuzangjing.

The *Shìshì tōngjiàn* differs from the contemporary [KR6r0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0012) in its non-sectarian stance: where [志磐](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BF%97%E7%A3%90)'s work is explicitly Tiāntái-centred, [本覺](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%AC%E8%A6%BA) presents a more even-handed treatment of Chán, Tiāntái, Vinaya, and doctrinal-school events. It is comparatively under-studied — overshadowed in modern scholarship by [志磐](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BF%97%E7%A3%90)'s and [念常](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BF%B5%E5%B8%B8)'s larger and more famous works — but is a useful comparative source for late-Sòng Buddhist historiography.
